Other days, I'll completely freeze in place holding a dish, or pace back and forth rubbing my hands and muttering prayers because I can't get my body to do what makes sense.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freeze in place, and how often they happen?\n\nPatient: These episodes have been happening almost every single day lately, or at least several times a week. It's a strange feeling because it's the exact opposite of those times when I completely freeze in place or feel like I'm moving through molasses. I just feel so weary and overwhelmed, like my body is completely out of my control.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where your symptoms, such as the feeling of moving through molasses or the episodes of pacing, have significantly improved or lifted, even if only for a short time, since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: There was a brief stretch late last summer when the heavy, sluggish feeling lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as tearful or low. Aside from that short time and a few scattered days, this heavy depression has been constant.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being tracked by people from the church and the hospital, and if you've experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: I keep thinking that people from the church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me for something. When the mail is late or the TV screen flickers, I take it as a sign that they are keeping tabs on me and sending me messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels so real to me and it just won't let up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail these signs you believe you're receiving and how they relate to your feelings of being punished or tracked by others?\n\nPatient: When the TV flickers, I feel like the hospital and church folks are sending coded signals to let me know they're watching my living room. If the mail is late, I'm convinced they've intercepted it to punish me for my wife's death, keeping tabs on everything I do. My sisters say it's just a coincidence, but it feels like a direct warning to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, in addition to believing you're receiving these signs and being tracked?\n\nPatient: No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?\n\nPatient: Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all \"crazy talk,\" the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?\n\nPatient: They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. But despite what my sisters tell me, the sense of being watched and receiving signs through the TV and mail feels completely real to me. It feels like an actual reality, not just something my mind is making up because I'm sad.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, and your own thoughts or feelings, and do you ever wonder if there could be another explanation for these events?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how to explain how I tell them apart, to be honest. The signs just feel completely real and external to me when they happen, like they are happening right in front of my eyes. I haven't really thought about any other explanations because it just feels so certain in the moment.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your feelings of being watched and receiving signs could be a part of your grief and sadness, rather than actual events happening to you?"

It’s like my body just locks up and refuses to cooperate, whether I'm trying to get out of bed or just standing in the living room holding a tool. It takes so much effort just to make myself move, and I end up just staring at the floor or pacing and muttering prayers to try and get going.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific thoughts or emotions that trigger these episodes of feeling like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?\n\nPatient: There isn't really a specific thought or trigger that starts it, honestly. It just feels like a physical disconnect where my body refuses to obey my mind, or my head goes completely blank and heavy. I just get stuck or move incredibly slow without any warning.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced any episodes of excessive and purposeless movement, like pacing back and forth, in addition to the episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?\n\nPatient: Yes, I do pace back and forth quite a bit, rubbing my hands together and muttering little bits of prayers under my breath because I can't make my body do anything that makes sense. It's a strange feeling because it's the exact opposite of those times when I completely freeze in place or feel like I'm moving through molasses. I just feel so weary and overwhelmed, like my body is completely out of my control.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where your symptoms, such as the feeling of moving through molasses or the episodes of pacing, have significantly improved or lifted, even if only for a short time, since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: There was a brief stretch late last summer when the heavy, sluggish feeling lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as tearful or low. Aside from that short time and a few scattered days, this heavy depression has been constant.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being tracked by people from the church and the hospital, and if you've experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: I keep thinking that people from the church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me for something. When the mail is late or the TV screen flickers, I take it as a sign that they are keeping tabs on me and sending me messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels so real to me and it just won't let up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail these signs you believe you're receiving and how they relate to your feelings of being punished or tracked by others?\n\nPatient: When the TV flickers, I feel like the hospital and church folks are sending coded signals to let me know they're watching my living room. If the mail is late, I'm convinced they've intercepted it to punish me for my wife's death, keeping tabs on everything I do. My sisters say it's just a coincidence, but it feels like a direct warning to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, in addition to believing you're receiving these signs and being tracked?\n\nPatient: No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?\n\nPatient: Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all \"crazy talk,\" the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?\n\nPatient: They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. But despite what my sisters tell me, the sense of being watched and receiving signs through the TV and mail feels completely real to me. It feels like an actual reality, not just something my mind is making up because I'm sad.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, and your own thoughts or feelings, and do you ever wonder if there could be another explanation for these events?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how to explain how I tell them apart, to be honest. The signs just feel completely real and external to me when they happen, like they are happening right in front of my eyes. I haven't really thought about any other explanations because it just feels so certain in the moment.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your feelings of being watched and receiving signs could be a part of your grief and sadness, rather than actual events happening to you?\n\nPatient: The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched did start around the same time, and they feel deeply tangled together. But even though my sisters call it \"crazy talk,\" I still truly believe the late mail and flickering TV are real signs that they are keeping tabs on me. It feels completely real, rather than just being a product of my grief.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, or if you've considered the possibility that they might be a product of your own mind rather than actual events?"

I just get stuck or move incredibly slow without any warning.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced any episodes of excessive and purposeless movement, like pacing back and forth, in addition to the episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?\n\nPatient: Yes, I do pace back and forth quite a bit, rubbing my hands together and muttering little bits of prayers under my breath because I can't make my body do anything that makes sense. It's a strange feeling because it's the exact opposite of those times when I completely freeze in place or feel like I'm moving through molasses. I just feel so weary and overwhelmed, like my body is completely out of my control.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where your symptoms, such as the feeling of moving through molasses or the episodes of pacing, have significantly improved or lifted, even if only for a short time, since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: There was a brief stretch late last summer when the heavy, sluggish feeling lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as tearful or low. But even during those weeks, I was still convinced that folks from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs. Aside from that short time and a few scattered days, this heavy depression has been constant.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being tracked by people from the church and the hospital, and if you've experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: I keep thinking that people from the church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me for something. When the mail is late or the TV screen flickers, I take it as a sign that they are keeping tabs on me and sending me messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels so real to me and it just won't let up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail these signs you believe you're receiving and how they relate to your feelings of being punished or tracked by others?\n\nPatient: When the TV flickers, I feel like the hospital and church folks are sending coded signals to let me know they're watching my living room. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?\n\nPatient: Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all \"crazy talk,\" the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?\n\nPatient: They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. It feels completely real, rather than just being a product of my grief.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, or if you've considered the possibility that they might be a product of your own mind rather than actual events?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had a moment of doubt because the signs feel completely real and solid when they happen. I just haven't been able to see it as something that's only in my head.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in being tracked and receiving signs could be related to the same feelings of sadness and grief that have been affecting you since your wife's passing, rather than being based on real events or messages from others?\n\nPatient: The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched are definitely deeply tangled together, and they both started right after my wife passed. But even if it is connected to my grief, those signs and the feeling of being watched still feel completely real and unsettling to me. No matter what others say, I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually keeping tabs on me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by an external force, or that you're being forced to think certain thoughts against your will?"

I usually just end up sitting in my recliner, staring at the wall.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: My appetite is pretty much gone, and I only really eat when my sister drops food off, though it just tastes like cardboard and my pants are hanging off me now. As for sleep, I mostly just lie awake in the dark with these heavy thoughts keeping me up.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or movement, such as feeling slowed down or restless, since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: Lately, it feels like I’m moving through molasses—getting from my bed to the bathroom takes forever, and I’ll just sit on the edge of the bed staring at the floor for fifteen minutes before my body finally stands up. Other days, I'll completely freeze in place holding a dish, or pace back and forth rubbing my hands and muttering prayers because I can't get my body to do what makes sense.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freeze in place, and how often they happen?\n\nPatient: These episodes have been happening almost every single day lately, or at least several times a week. It’s like my body just locks up and refuses to cooperate, whether I'm trying to get out of bed or just standing in the living room holding a tool. It takes so much effort just to make myself move, and I end up just staring at the floor or pacing and muttering prayers to try and get going.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific thoughts or emotions that trigger these episodes of feeling like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?\n\nPatient: There isn't really a specific thought or trigger that starts it, honestly. It just feels like a physical disconnect where my body refuses to obey my mind, or my head goes completely blank and heavy. I just get stuck or move incredibly slow without any warning.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced any episodes of excessive and purposeless movement, like pacing back and forth, in addition to the episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?\n\nPatient: Yes, I do pace back and forth quite a bit, rubbing my hands together and muttering little bits of prayers under my breath because I can't make my body do anything that makes sense. It's a strange feeling because it's the exact opposite of those times when I completely freeze in place or feel like I'm moving through molasses. I just feel so weary and overwhelmed, like my body is completely out of my control.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where your symptoms, such as the feeling of moving through molasses or the episodes of pacing, have significantly improved or lifted, even if only for a short time, since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: There was a brief stretch late last summer when the heavy, sluggish feeling lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as tearful or low. But even during those weeks, I was still convinced that folks from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs. Aside from that short time and a few scattered days, this heavy depression has been constant.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being tracked by people from the church and the hospital, and if you've experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions since your wife's passing?\n\nPatient: I keep thinking that people from the church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me for something. When the mail is late or the TV screen flickers, I take it as a sign that they are keeping tabs on me and sending me messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels so real to me and it just won't let up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail these signs you believe you're receiving and how they relate to your feelings of being punished or tracked by others?\n\nPatient: When the TV flickers, I feel like the hospital and church folks are sending coded signals to let me know they're watching my living room. If the mail is late, I'm convinced they've intercepted it to punish me for my wife's death, keeping tabs on everything I do. My sisters say it's just a coincidence, but it feels like a direct warning to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, in addition to believing you're receiving these signs and being tracked?\n\nPatient: No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?\n\nPatient: Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all \"crazy talk,\" the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?\n\nPatient: They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. But despite what my sisters tell me, the sense of being watched and receiving signs through the TV and mail feels completely real to me. It feels like an actual reality, not just something my mind is making up because I'm sad.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, and your own thoughts or feelings, and do you ever wonder if there could be another explanation for these events?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how to explain how I tell them apart, to be honest. The signs just feel completely real and external to me when they happen, like they are happening right in front of my eyes. I haven't really thought about any other explanations because it just feels so certain in the moment.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your feelings of being watched and receiving signs could be a part of your grief and sadness, rather than actual events happening to you?\n\nPatient: The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched did start around the same time, and they feel deeply tangled together. But even though my sisters call it \"crazy talk,\" I still truly believe the late mail and flickering TV are real signs that they are keeping tabs on me. It feels completely real, rather than just being a product of my grief.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, or if you've considered the possibility that they might be a product of your own mind rather than actual events?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had a moment of doubt because the signs feel completely real and solid when they happen. Even though my sisters keep telling me it's just \"crazy talk,\" I truly believe the late mail and the flickering TV are actual messages they're sending me. I just haven't been able to see it as something that's only in my head.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in being tracked and receiving signs could be related to the same feelings of sadness and grief that have been affecting you since your wife's passing, rather than being based on real events or messages from others?\n\nPatient: The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched are definitely deeply tangled together, and they both started right after my wife passed. No matter what others say, I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually keeping tabs on me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by an external force, or that you're being forced to think certain thoughts against your will?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my actual thoughts are being controlled or that anyone is putting thoughts into my head. It's more that I feel like they are watching me from the outside and sending me messages through the TV and the mail. My own thoughts still feel like my own.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a moment where you felt like your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs were not true, or if you have always been completely convinced of their reality?\n\nPatient: I have always been completely convinced that it is real, and I've never really had a single moment of doubt. Even though my sisters keep telling me it's just \"crazy talk,\" when the TV flickers or the mail is late, it feels 100% real to me. I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually keeping tabs on me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you were to feel better and your sadness were to lift, you would still believe that people from the church and hospital are tracking you and sending you signs?\n\nPatient: Yes, I believe I would still feel that way, because I actually had a period late last summer when my mood lifted slightly and I wasn't feeling as deeply depressed or tearful. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?\n\nPatient: Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all \"crazy talk,\" the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?\n\nPatient: They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. But despite what my sisters tell me, the sense of being watched and receiving signs through the TV and mail feels completely real to me. It feels like an actual reality, not just something my mind is making up because I'm sad.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, and your own thoughts or feelings, and do you ever wonder if there could be another explanation for these events?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how to explain how I tell them apart, to be honest. It feels completely real, rather than just being a product of my grief.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, or if you've considered the possibility that they might be a product of your own mind rather than actual events?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had a moment of doubt because the signs feel completely real and solid when they happen. Even though my sisters keep telling me it's just \"crazy talk,\" I truly believe the late mail and the flickering TV are actual messages they're sending me.
